title: PioneerGrid - Onboarding Activation Huddle
summary: Kickoff/handoff to implementation: reviewed network/VPC needs, key success criteria (latency < 300ms for core routes, PII routing rules), pilot scope for two endpoints, and next steps for security docs and test credentials.
topics: Pilot model selection and quantization tradeoffs
action_items: Lena Ortiz - Share internal list of expected peak QPS and representative payload sizes - 2026-02-03
Dante Ruiz - Run initial perf baseline (hosted vs dedicated) and share results - 2026-02-05
Tasha Imani - Provide PioneerGrid security questionnaire answers and KMS details - 2026-02-02
Priya Shah - Send onboarding runbook and staging checklist, include tenant mapping template - 2026-01-29
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding runbook + security pack (Priya)
Customer to provision test VPC peering and temp credentials (Lena)
SE to run baseline perf tests and return spreadsheet (Dante)
Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2/9 once VPC and creds validated
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-01-27 15:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Dante Ruiz (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz, Mark Feldman, Tasha Imani, Ibrahim Khan (PioneerGrid)
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick agenda — handoff from sales to success, confirm pilot scope and security gating, and outline next 2 weeks. Is that good?
00:18 Lena: Yeah that's perfect. We mainly want to validate perf and make sure data doesn't leave our VPC. Also timeline is tight, aiming for initial pilot by mid-February.
00:34 Jordan: Great, thanks. Priya, quick intro from success side?

00:38 Priya: Hi all — I'll be your CSM during onboarding, primary contact for scheduling and runbook items. We'll also coordinate with Diana in Ops if needed. Small note: we prefer weekly 30 minute standups during ramp.
00:55 Mark: Sounds good, 30 minutes works. For SRE we'll need specifics on egress and peering, plus what ports the runtime opens.

01:10 Dante: Sure — for hosted we only need outbound to Redwood API on 443, but for Private/Dedicated we might require peering and a couple internal ports for health checks. We'll send the exact list in the runbook.

01:30 Tasha: From security — we'll be looking for SOC2 evidence, KMS integration options, and whether Redwood rotates keys or if we manage them. Also audit log retention requirements; we have 7 years for some data classes.

01:47 Jordan: On SOC2 we have our report and our SOC auditor contact; we'll attach the certs. For KMS you can pick either customer-managed keys in KMS or Redwood-managed — Dante can go over tradeoffs.

02:05 Dante: Right — customer-managed KMS gives you full control over rotation and access but requires some extra setup on peering and IAM roles. For pilot we can do a 'bring your own KMS' path or a quick temp key for baseline tests.
02:25 Ibrahim: Quick Q — does the hosted API ever cache any raw inputs? Need to check PII handling for compliance.
02:32 Priya: By default hosted API has default retention policies; we can disable retention for your account during pilot. We'll confirm in the security pack. That's an important gating item.

03:00 Jordan: Ok moving to pilot scope — we propose two endpoints: 1) low-latency short-chat route for customer support triage, 2) batch embeddings for search indexing. Target is to prove latency under 300ms 95th for the chat route and embedding throughput at X qps.

03:22 Lena: That matches our priorities. Our current search pipeline expects embeddings at 20 qps with 1-2 second batching latency tolerated. The chat is more sensitive. We need to see cost delta between hosted and a small dedicated pool.

03:40 Dante: We'll run comparisons: hosted baseline, then a dedicated 2-GPU config with quantization options. Expect to see ~30-40% token cost reduction with 4-bit quantization but need to validate quality on your prompts.
04:02 Mark: For dedicated, what's the SLA and burst options? If we have daily traffic spikes we can't have degraded response times.

04:10 Jordan: Dedicated pools come with commit sizing and burst, and we can set up fallback to hosted if capacity is exceeded. We'll document SLOs in the contract; Priya will follow up with the exact latency SLA tiers.
04:28 Tasha: Also can you describe tracing hooks? We need distributed tracing to map requests to our X-Ray/Jaeger stack.
04:35 Amber: We expose trace IDs and have an agent for forwarding traces; we can map to Jaeger and instrument spans. We'll attach sample tracing headers in the runbook.
05:02 Lena: Ok good. On the network side, we need a list of CIDR ranges for egress and any IP allowlist. We also will lock down egress so only necessary endpoints are allowed.
05:20 Dante: We'll provide a minimal allowlist for pilot. If you go Private, traffic stays in your VPC and you control egress entirely.
06:00 Jordan: One sticky point — data residency. Some of your user data must remain in EU. You're US+EU, correct?
06:08 Lena: Yes, mostly EU for our EU customers. We'll need region pinning and assurances about model routing.
06:15 Priya: Redwood supports region routing; we can pin the model to eu-west-1 for EU traffic. We'll add that to the pilot plan.
06:30 Ibrahim: Perf baseline logistics — what do you need from us to run realistic tests?

06:36 Dante: Something representative: 1) a sample set of prompt templates and percentile lengths, 2) auth credentials or a temporary test API key, 3) expected concurrency patterns. If you share a small sample corpus and synthetic load shape we'll mirror it.
07:05 Lena: I'll share a sanitized prompt set and expected QPS by next Tuesday. We'll also provide a short list of edge-case prompts that often degrade quality.
07:22 Jordan: Excellent. On evals — we can run automatic quality regression tests against your prompt set and send a before/after for quantization and model switches.
07:35 Mark: Regarding logs, what's included in audit logs? We need request IDs, timestamps, user IDs (anonymized), model version, and tokens consumed for billing reconciliation.
07:46 Priya: We capture request metadata and model version in the audit logs; we can also push aggregated token usage by route. We will confirm the exact schema in the docs.
08:05 Tasha: Encryption in transit and at rest, is that standard? And for on-prem do you support HSMs?

08:12 Amber: Yes TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. For private/on-prem we integrate with customer HSMs or cloud KMS; we'll note supported vendors. There's a small engineering setup for HSM cert exchange.

08:30 Jordan: Switching to timeline: we propose this plan — this week: security questionnaire and VPC details, next week: provide test creds and Redwood runs perf baselines, week after: pilot kickoff and initial run. Does that align?
08:50 Lena: That aligns. We have an internal freeze on infra changes the first week of Feb, so best to complete perf baselines before then.
09:05 Dante: We'll prioritize baseline this week once you hand over sample prompts and temporary creds. Might take 48-72 hours to run and analyze.
09:20 Mark: On cost — curious about token-based billing vs reserved capacity for the pilot. Any quick estimate?

09:27 Jordan: For a short pilot, token-based hosted billing is simplest. We'll include a cost estimate for dedicated once we see QPS. Often dedicated becomes economical after a steady threshold; we'll include model-size and quantization sensitivity in that analysis.
09:45 Lena: We also need an internal stakeholder map — who owns prod cutover and who signs off on compliance?
09:52 Tasha: Security is owner for compliance sign-off, but CTO signs final go/no-go. We'll share the approvals matrix.
10:10 Priya: Great — I'll capture the approvals matrix in the runbook template. Also, we recommend two staging tenants to mirror EU/US separation.
10:30 Jordan: Any blockers right now from customer's side?
10:34 Mark: The only blocker is network calendar alignment for a short maintenance window to test peering, and getting security questionnaire answers. Everything else is logistical.
10:48 Lena: We'll prioritize peering window and aim to send the security pack by Monday.
11:05 Dante: One technical nuance — for embeddings we recommend batched requests of up to 32 items to reduce per-embedding latency; we'll provide code samples for batching and local prefetch caching.
11:28 Ibrahim: That helps. We'll integrate batching in our ingest lambda and test.
11:45 Jordan: Alright before we close let's quickly recap actions and owners...

12:00 Priya: Recap: Priya to share runbook/security pack and tenant mapping template; Lena to share sample prompts and QPS; Tasha to push security questionnaire; Dante to run perf baselines and share spreadsheet; Jordan to send cost/option overview for hosted vs dedicated. Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2/9 pending peering/credentials.
12:35 Lena: Good recap. One last question: can we do a short technical deep-dive with Redwood infra folks after baseline? Maybe 30 minutes.
12:45 Jordan: Absolutely — we'll schedule a technical deep-dive with the infra/SE team for the week after baselines. I'll coordinate calendars.
13:05 Tasha: Thanks everyone. We'll be in touch with questionnaire and creds.
13:12 Jordan: Thanks all — meeting adjourned.
44:30 (end of recording)
